ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, and beneficial owners against the Canadian Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UK HM Treasury Sanctions List, and EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List. Enhanced due diligence required for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) under FINTRAC AML/CFT regulations and Alberta's Beneficial Ownership Registrar mandates. Screening must be renewed annually or upon change in ownership directly from government repositories using identity verification tools.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (via the Province of Alberta online portal at https://www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names may be expressed in English, French, or a combination, using Latin script. Transliterations of non-Latin names must be provided in English or French and must include a mandatory legal element (Corporation, Incorporated, Limited, Corp., Inc., Ltd., or Limitée). Names must be distinct from existing Alberta corporate, registered trade union, or extra-provincial registrations. A NUANS name search is mandatory for all proposed corporate names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant receives a written notice from the Alberta Corporate Registry. The applicant may submit a written reconsideration request to the Director of Corporate Registry within 30 days of the rejection notice. The request must include the original NUANS report, a comparison of the reasoning for the confusion, and any supporting evidence (e.g., consent from the conflicting name holder). If the Director overturns the rejection, the name will be reserved for the initial 90-day period from the original reservation date. Alternatively, the applicant may file a fresh NUANS search and name registration using a different proposed name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible provided it is a physical street address in Alberta (not a PO Box) capable of accepting registered mail and service of process. The registered office must be accessible for personal service during ordinary business hours. A commercial virtual office service with a dedicated street address and mail handling is acceptable for a low-risk e-commerce business such as custom keyboard cap manufacturing and sales.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate. Estimated 10-15% annual probability of an unannounced compliance inspection by municipal or provincial authorities, given the e-commerce retail model and absence of regulated activities. Physical-inspection risk is primarily limited to general Corporate Registry verification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended, ss. 6 (manner of incorporation), 8 (articles of incorporation), 10 (certificate of incorporation), 101 (registered office) and 113 (notice of directors); alternative federal route available under the Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, ss. 5-8, with extra-provincial registration in Alberta.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction Division, Government of Alberta (online filing via an accredited Corporate Registry Online service provider).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1, Alberta); the Certificate of Incorporation is issued electronically by the Director of the Alberta Corporate Registry after statutory review.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the ABCA; shares may be issued for cash or other consideration determined by the directors, and no paid-up capital escrow or bank lock-up account is required for an Alberta provincial business corporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the Corporation accept subscriptions and issue the initial shares under the capitalization schedule, credited fully paid upon receipt of consideration; (2) that the registered office be fixed per the filed Notice of Registered Office, appointing the records office; (3) that the first Bylaws of the Corporation be adopted; (4) that [Name] be appointed President, [Name] Treasurer/CFO, and [Name] Corporate Secretary; (5) that signatories be authorized to open a commercial bank account and execute Shopify Payments and Stripe processing agreements; (6) that management file post-incorporation returns and obtain municipal and environmental clearances; (7) that all prior incorporation acts be ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and NUANS Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via an accredited NUANS search service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) request for the proposed corporate name; review the search report for identical or confusingly similar names; if the proposed name is clear, reserve the name for 90 days, or alternatively adopt a numbered Alberta corporation name until a trade-name registration is completed.
required_dossiers: Completed NUANS name search request form
Proposed corporate name and jurisdiction preference
Payment for the NUANS search and reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Corporate Registry rejects the proposed name on distinctiveness or confusion grounds, file a written request for re-consideration with distinguishing marks and supporting trademark evidence within 15 days, or amend the name request and re-submit; use a numbered company name as a fallback to avoid delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Articles of Incorporation and Initial Corporate Governance Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) including the authorized share structure, restrictions on share transfers (if any), number of directors, and the registered office address; draft the initial by-laws, unanimous shareholder agreement (if applicable), capital schedule, share certificate specimens and consents to act as director; obtain signatures of the incorporator as required by s. 6 of the ABCA.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation (Form 1)
NUANS name reservation confirmation
Initial by-laws and unanimous shareholder agreement drafts
Consent to act as director for each proposed director
Share capitalization schedule and certificate specimens
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or counsel identifies drafting deficiencies, amend the governing documents and re-execute all signature pages; any registry query must be answered within 5 business days after receipt of the requisition.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of Articles of Incorporation with Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry Online (Service Alberta) or an accredited service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the authorized Corporate Registry Online portal, upload the signed Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) and the NUANS report aged less than 90 days, pay the C$50 electronic filing fee, and receive an acknowledgment and provisional filing number; the Director of the Corporate Registry will review the application and issue the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Signed Articles of Incorporation (Form 1)
Valid NUANS name search report
Proof of filing fee payment
Corresponding corporate records book and minute book templates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry returns the filing for completeness corrections, cure the defect within 30 days of the notice and re-submit the corrected Form 1; the filing fee is applied to the re-filed version and no additional fee is levied if corrected within the same filing cycle.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Adoption of First Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directors of the Corporation at the organizational meeting (with the corporate minute book)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, convene the organizational meeting of directors; adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution covering share allotment and subscription, adoption of by-laws, confirmation of the registered office, appointment of officers, bank account opening, and approval of the Shopify Payments and Stripe payment-processor agreements; issue share certificates and record the capitalization schedule in the securities register.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by Alberta Corporate Registry
Approved First Board Resolution and organizational meeting minutes
Blood director consents and by-laws
Capitalization schedule and share register
Bank account and payment processor resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any director consent is defective or missing, obtain a corrected consent and file it immediately in the corporate records; if any shares are not fully paid, the directors must either collect the unpaid consideration or cancel the allotment in accordance with s. 25 and the capitalization schedule.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Filing of Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, Government of Alberta (online filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days after the date of the Certificate of Incorporation, file Form 2 (Notice of Registered Office) and Form 3 (Notice of Directors) through the Corporate Registry Online portal, providing the Alberta physical municipality address of the registered office (post office boxes not permitted) and the full names and addresses of all appointed directors; retain the stamped notices in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Form 2 - Notice of Registered Office
Form 3 - Notice of Directors
Consents to act as directors (filed in the corporate records)
Registered office address validation documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notices are queried or rejected due to incomplete information, withdraw and re-file the corrected Form 2 and Form 3 promptly; if the 15-day statutory deadline is missed, file a late-filing request and rely on the Minister's discretion to accept the notice, subject to any late filing penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Municipal Development Permit and Business Licence for the Manufacturing Premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Planning and Development Department and Business Licensing Office of the operating municipality (City of Calgary or City of Edmonton, as applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a development permit for light manufacturing use at the selected premises, confirming the zoning permits plastic injection molding operations; submit a site plan showing the molding presses, material storage areas and egress routes; upon issuance of the development permit, apply for the municipal business licence and remit the annual licence fee; update the licence when the registered business address or commercial trade name changes after Shopify Payments and Stripe onboarding.
required_dossiers: Zoning certificate for the proposed manufacturing site
Development permit application and site plan
Floor load and structural layout details for injection molding machinery
Municipal business licence application and fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the development permit is refused or imposes excessive conditions, appeal to the Subdivision and Development Appeal Board within 21 days of the decision; alternatively amend the site plan to comply with the municipality's land use requirements and re-file the amended application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical Premises Inspection, Fire Safety Clearance, Occupational Health Clearance and Environmental Self-Assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Municipal Affairs (Safety Codes Act accredited agencies), Alberta Occupational Health and Safety, and Alberta Environment and Protected Areas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Retain an accredited safety codes agency to perform the electrical and fire safety inspection of the manufacturing premises under the Alberta Fire Code and the Safety Codes Act; obtain the fire safety certificate and electrical installation clearance before commencing production; complete an OHS workplace hazard assessment covering machine guarding, noise exposure, lockout/tagout and PBT plastic dust controls; carry out an environmental screening self-assessment under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act to determine whether the facility falls below the EPEA approval threshold; if the facility is exempt, maintain records of VOC emissions, wastewater discharge and plastic waste manifests.
required_dossiers: Fire safety inspection report and certificate from an accredited safety codes agency
Electrical installation clearance certificate
Occupational Health and Safety hazard assessment and clearance
Environmental screening self-assessment and EPEA registration determination
Waste management and discharge records (if thresholds are exceeded)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a safety codes officer issues a nonconformity order, abate the identified defect and request a re-inspection within 5 to 10 business days; if the environmental screening determines that an EPEA approval is required, retain a qualified environmental consultant, complete an environmental impact assessment report, and obtain the formal approval before commencing full production.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Municipal Affairs (Safety Services Division) together with the Planning and Development Department of the operating municipality (City of Calgary or City of Edmonton); no separate provincial manufacturing licence is required for ISIC 3240 plastic injection molding under Alberta law.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence for a light-manufacturing facility, supplemented by the Safety Codes Act fire and electrical certificates and the Canada Revenue Agency Business Number (BN) registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Registration / Exempt: small-scale plastic injection molding with VOC emissions below the mandatory approval thresholds is exempt from a full Environmental Impact Assessment under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, but the facility must complete a screening self-assessment and register with the AEPA if the release limits are exceeded.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to municipal sewers must comply with the municipality's sewer-use by-law (typically pH 6.0 to 9.0, total suspended solids not exceeding 350 mg/L, and no visible plastic pellets or resin solids); air emissions from molding machines are capped at 20 tonnes per year of volatile organic compounds and 500 kg per year of hazardous air pollutants, with annual emissions reporting to the AEPA if exceeded; plastic trimming waste must be segregated and transported with a waste manifest under EPEA if sent offsite for recycling or disposal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification obtained under the Alberta Fire Code and the Safety Codes Act after inspection of the molding floor, storage and egress; structural load inspection certifying the floor capacity for injection molding presses; electrical installation clearance from an accredited safety codes agency; and an Occupational Health and Safety clearance under the Alberta OHS Act, Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Code, covering machine guarding, noise reduction, lockout/tagout and workplace hazard controls.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Canada's federal tax administration for GST/HST and corporate income tax; Alberta provincial corporate income tax is also administered by the CRA under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act; official portals include CRA My Business Account and Business Registration Online; export administration is shared with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Alberta business corporation must first incorporate under the Alberta Business Corporations Act or the Canada Business Corporations Act, satisfy registered-office and resident-director requirements, and obtain its Alberta corporate registry file. The corporation then applies for a 9-digit CRA Business Number (BN) and the required program accounts for GST/HST, payroll, and import/export through CRA Business Registration Online or Form RC1. A separate GST/HST registration account uses the BN followed by an 'RT' account code. Non-resident corporations without a Canadian permanent establishment may also apply for a non-resident GST/HST account under the Excise Tax Act, using Form RC1 and supporting foreign-entity documents, if they carry on business in Canada or voluntarily register to claim input tax credits.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide United States-style check-the-box elections or a separate hybrid-mismatch entity election. A legal corporation is always treated as a separate taxpayer subject to entity-level corporate income tax and cannot elect pass-through treatment. Relevant statutory elections in this context include: Income Tax Act section 85 rollover elections for tax-deferred transfers of property into the corporation, GST/HST related-party elections under ETA section 156 for closely related corporations, and certain capital cost allowance pooling elections. Hybrid mismatch outcomes are constrained by Canadian residency rules, the general anti-avoidance rule under Income Tax Act section 245, and transfer-pricing rules; no elective Canadian domestic hybrid-mismatch check-the-box regime exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) — federal value-added tax; Alberta has no provincial sales tax or PST, so the effective indirect tax rate in Alberta is the 5% federal GST only.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — the GST/HST small-supplier threshold measured by global taxable supplies, including those of associated persons, in the four consecutive calendar quarters ending before registration; exporters exceeding this threshold while carrying on business in Canada must register for GST/HST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no real-time tax authority invoice clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory Peppol-style e-invoicing regime as of the current tax period. CRA accepts electronic invoices and books and records where they are retained in readable format. GST/HST registrants must issue prescribed tax-invoice information and may file returns electronically through CRA's GST/HST Internet File Transfer service. There is no API-based per-invoice fiscal approval obligation; however, for export transactions the registrant must retain shipment and payment documentation sufficient to substantiate the zero-rated supply on audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A registered Alberta exporter may zero-rate custom mechanical keyboard keycaps under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, as tangible personal property exported in a continuous journey to a destination outside Canada, or delivered to a common carrier for export. The supply must be made to a non-resident buyer and physically leave Canada. Supporting services supplied to the non-resident buyer in relation to the exported goods may also be zero-rated if they are not performed in Canada or are not in connection with Canadian real property or Canadian tangible personal property. The exporter claims input tax credits for GST paid on manufacturing inputs on its regular GST/HST return; no separate export refund application is required. Although Canada imposes no explicit statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline, 180 days after shipment is the standard commercial and audit benchmark for receiving export proceeds; extended non-payment or related-party delayed settlement materially increases CRA scrutiny of whether a genuine export sale occurred.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA export declaration (Form B13A or Canadian Automated Export Declaration data) where the shipment value exceeds CAD 2,000 or the goods are controlled, regulated, or require a permit
Commercial invoice in English or French describing the keycaps, quantity, export classification, country of origin, seller, buyer, and consideration
Packing list showing exact shipment contents, weights, and destination
Bill of lading or airway waybill evidencing physical carriage from Canada to the foreign consignee
Inward remittance evidence from the foreign buyer, such as a SWIFT MT103, bank credit advice, or letter of credit settlement record
Customs broker or carrier electronic release/export confirmation confirming actual exit of the goods from Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess a GST/HST return within four years from the date originally filed, and the limitation period is unlimited where the registrant has made a misrepresentation or committed fraud or wilful neglect. If zero-rating is disallowed for lack of export evidence, the 5% GST is clawed back from the Canadian exporter as uncollected net tax, plus prescribed daily compound interest. False or grossly negligent statements can trigger penalties under ETA section 280, generally the greater of CAD 100 and 25% of the net-tax shortfall, with additional penalties under the Customs Act for inaccurate export declarations. Knowingly evading GST/HST or facilitating a false export claim is a criminal offence under ETA section 327 and may result in substantial fines and imprisonment, in addition to full recovery of tax, interest, and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as the monetary authority, with foreign exchange policy administered under the Currency Act; FINTRAC serves as the financial intelligence and AML/CTF supervisor for authorized foreign exchange and money services businesses.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current and capital account convertibility. The Canadian dollar is a freely floating and widely traded currency. There are no exchange control, surrender, or approval requirements for capital inflows, current payments, or profit remittances by non-residents. The only legal constraints arise from U.N./automated sanctions screening, FINTRAC large-transaction reporting (C$10,000), and Canada Revenue Agency rules on the functional currency of foreign-denominated earnings.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender rule or mandatory repatriation timeline exists for Canadian exporters. Export receipts may remain in foreign currency, though they must be valued in Canadian dollars for income tax and GST/HST purposes. FINTRAC reportable transactions apply at C$10,000 per payment. Payments from sanctioned jurisdictions or involving dual-use goods are restricted under the Special Economic Measures Act and Export and Import Permits Act.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-high operational viability as a supplementary settlement corridor, but low legal viability as a full replacement for a Schedule I Canadian chartered bank. Offshore EMI accounts (e.g., E.U./U.K.-based EMI licenses) are not recognized as Canadian bank accounts; they may be used only for payment collection in foreign platform ecosystems, with fund flows passed into a regulated Canadian account. Stripe and Shopify Payments are the preferred fintech rails, subject to their own KYC and merchant underwriting, but a domestic bank account and FINTRAC registration are still necessary for treasury control and large-volume settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance by directors is not universally mandated if the corporation has a registered Alberta office and directors hold verifiable identity. Major banks permit remote or video-based KYC for low-risk manufacturing/exporting entities, supplemented by a notarized authorization resolution and corporate registry search. However, branch discretion may require an in-person visit for accounts holding capital escrow funds, when a director is a non-resident with no Canadian credit history, or where the beneficial owner resides in a FATF high-risk jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director or ultimate beneficial owner with tax residence in a high-risk or sanctioned jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized passports or permanent resident cards, proof of tax-residency certificates, certified corporate registry records, source-of-wealth statements, bank references from correspondent institutions, and third-party adverse-media or sanctions screening reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume low-unit-value exports to third-party fulfillment centers creating a trade-based money-laundering red flag
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoices and packing lists, HW/HS classifications, export customs declarations, freight-forwarder or courier tracking data, purchase orders, Shopify/Stripe settlement ledgers, inventory purchase records, and audited sales pipeline documentation for the custom keycap manufacturing activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusually rapid account activation after only a nominal capitalization threshold or high proportion of incoming funds from unregulated PSPs
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan with projected cash flows, third-party verified supplier and customer contracts, unit economics for double-shot PBT manufacturing, share subscription documents, and a written commitment to maintain an operational no-crypto/no-cash policy in the corporate account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from foreign shareholders are routed as SWIFT MT103 wires into a Canadian Chartered Bank account, using the exact legal corporate name and the CC (Canadian clearing code) along with the Bank/Institution, Branch, and Account number. Remittance instructions should reference the share subscription agreement or shareholder subordinated loan; the note field must identify the transaction as 'Capital Injection' or 'Equity Contribution'. Wires equal to or above C$10,000 trigger FINTRAC large-transaction reporting. For larger foreign investments, a post-closing Investment Canada Act notification may be required; capital injection into a wholly-owned Alberta operating company is generally exempt from pre-merger review.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Productive cross-border disbursements for tooling moulds, double-shot PBT resin pellets, keycap stems, and specialized fixtures are cleared through SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers to supplier accounts, with CAD-to-USD execution provided at the bank’s competitive rate. For high-value custom molds, a commercial documentary letter of credit under UCP600 with an advising bank in the toolmaker’s country is recommended. Domestic Alberta supplier payments are settled via the Canadian Payments Association / Real-Time Rail (RTR) e-transfer or batch ACH; all outbound wires must pass OFAC, UN, and Canadian sanctions screening before execution.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Cross-currency interest rate swaps between CAD and USD

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: filing is due no later than one month after the anniversary of incorporation or amalgamation; e.g., an anniversary of March 15 requires filing on or before April 15.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years may trigger administrative dissolution by the Registrar after notice; reinstatement requires filing all missed returns, paying reinstatement fees, and may require Registrar consent. A delinquent corporation cannot obtain a certificate of status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return with financial statements and reconcilement schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the taxation year-end; quarterly corporate income tax instalments are due on the last day of each quarter where the corporation has tax payable above the statutory instalment threshold.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a 5% penalty on unpaid tax plus 1% per full month of delay up to 12 months; repeat offenders face a 10% penalty plus 2% per month up to 20 months. Interest accrues on unpaid amounts, and director liability may arise for unremitted source deductions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue-based audit threshold applies to Alberta private corporations. An independent auditor must be appointed for each shareholders' meeting unless all shareholders of a non-distributing corporation consent in writing to waive the auditor. Distributing corporations are always required to appoint an independent auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian accounting framework: IFRS is required for publicly accountable enterprises; private corporations may use IFRS or ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises, Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Alberta annual return is the statutory confirmation event, confirming the registered office address and the current directors. Alberta does not currently require a separate annual UBO declaration filing for ordinary private corporations; however, any transfer of shares must be recorded in the Register of Members and directors must be updated promptly. If the corporation is governed by the Canada Business Corporations Act, a register of individuals with significant control must be maintained and made available for inspection, although it is not separately filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 100-350 per annum (typical Alberta registered agent and registered office maintenance, including compliance calendar tracking)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000-10,000 per annum for a small Alberta private manufacturing/trading corporation; reduced if a review engagement or Notice to Reader is available by shareholder waiver.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined federal and Alberta general corporate rate of 23% (federal 15% + Alberta 8%). A Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) benefits from the small business deduction, producing an 11% combined rate on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income; a subsidiary controlled by non-residents is not a CCPC and is taxed at the flat 23% general rate.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal small business deduction (19% reduction, 9% rate, first CAD 500,000 active business income); Alberta small business deduction (2% rate on first CAD 500,000); SR&ED investment tax credits (35% refundable CCDP/40%? no — 35% refundable for CCPCs up to the expenditure limit, 15% non-refundable otherwise); accelerated CCA Class 43 (30% DB) for plastic injection moulding machinery; immediate expensing of qualifying manufacturing and processing equipment up to CAD 1,500,000 (federal); Alberta has no provincial sales tax (GST only, 5%).
